stem.en: The graph shows the acceleration that one force gives to objects of different masses. A 1 kg object gets 10 m/s², and a 5 kg object gets 2 m/s². What does the force-mass graph look like?

text.en: A straight line rising from the origin

feedback.en: Work out F = ma for two points. The force does not grow with the mass.
Right. 1 kg x 10 m/s² = 10 N and 5 kg x 2 m/s² = 10 N. The force is the same for every mass.

text.en: A falling curve, like the graph shown

feedback.en: The acceleration falls as the mass grows, but the force F = ma stays the same.
Check F = ma at 1 kg: 1 kg x 10 m/s² = 10 N.

explanation.en: The same force acts on every object. From F = ma: 1 kg x 10 m/s² = 10 N, and 5 kg x 2 m/s² = 10 N. So the force-mass graph is a flat line at 10 N.

hints.en: Find F = ma at two points of the graph.
